t: You're in Bermondsey Square, once the heart of Bermondsey Abbey, an English Benedictine monastery. It is generally regarded as founded in the eleventh century, though an earlier community is mentioned in the early eighth. Two royal figures are tied to the abbey. Henry the Young King, eldest surviving son of Henry II, was born here. He was crowned in his father's lifetime, and died at twenty-eight. Catherine of Valois, queen of Henry V and mother of Henry VI, died here in 1437. The abbey itself is gone, but the market now trades on its site.
